earlier_scan.source_named: Kumar, Braj Bihari. 1972. Pocuri vyakarana ki ruparekha [Outline of Pochury grammar]. Kohima: Nagaland Bhasha Parishad. 28pp.
earlier_scan.note: Only known sketch (28pp, Hindi); not digitized anywhere reachable; Shodhganga could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page poch1243 and reference pages 85928, 661069; Hammarström hh.bib (copy consulted).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: one descriptive ref (Kumar 1972 sketch); additional non-descriptive refs naming Pochuri: Mills 1937, Marrison 1967, Ezung & Walling 2020, Saul 2005, Stirn & van Ham 2003, Coupe 2012 (subclassification).

sources.citation: Shodhganga@INFLIBNET searches: 'Pochury', 'Pochuri' (14 hits, 2 pages), 'Meluri language', 'Pochury phonology'.
sources.note: No thesis on Pochury language exists in Shodhganga; hits are anthropology/history (Pojar 2022 dental morphometrics; Chukhapa 2023 polity) and other Naga languages (Poula, Zeme/Liangmai/Rongmei, Tangkhul).

sources.citation: Debnath, Rupak. 2023. Rengma Dialects. Self-deposited 3-page paper, archive.org identifier rengma-dialects.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that Mills (1937:288ff) "provided the only available data on the language spoken in Meluri" and that Marrison (1967) "systematically analyses Mills' data on Meluri"; gives a 32-item Meluri wordlist copied from Mills. About Rengma proper (Nzang/Nzon), not Pochuri.

sources.citation: Teo, Amos. 2014. A phonological and phonetic description of Sumi, a Tibeto-Burman language of Nagaland. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics. Section 8.4.1, Table 38 (tone systems of Angami-Pochuri and Ao languages).
sources.note: Nothing on Pochuri specifically: the comparative tone table covers Khezha, Chokri, Mao, Angami (Khonoma, Kohima), Sumi, Ao, Lotha; Pochuri is not among the languages tabulated. States generally that Angami-Pochuri-group languages have three to five lexical tones.

sources.citation: Mills, J. P. 1937. The Rengma Nagas. London: Macmillan. Part VI "Language", pp. 285-301ff (Language C = Eastern Rengma of Meluri, Lephori, Sahunyu = Pochuri).
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. The language outline (three languages A, B, C; C = Meluri/Eastern Rengma) says only: "I have used no diacritical marks, and tones have only been noted where of special importance. Only syllables which are very strongly long or short have been so marked." (p. 287); tone remarked as of "great importance" only for language B (p. 290 fn.). a full-text search for stress/accent/intonation in the whole text finds no linguistic use.
No phonology; lists dialects (Pochuri, Maluri/Meluri; Müluori, Phorü, Yisi, Apoksha, Phongkhungri, Samburi, Kuki) and cites only census figures, van Driem 2011 and Kloss & McConnell 1989.

sources.note: The only descriptive sketch of Pochuri in Glottolog; a 28-page Hindi outline of this series typically opens with a sound-system section (varṇa-vyavasthā) that may state tone and/or stress (balāghāt).

sources.citation: Ezung, Mimi Kevichüsa & Pangersenla Walling. 2020. Typology of the Naga Languages: A Pilot Study. Kohima: Department of Art & Culture, Government of Nagaland. v+219 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Recent comparative survey by Nagaland University linguists that explicitly includes Pochury among 17 Naga languages; a typological pilot study of this kind normally tabulates phoneme inventories, tone and suprasegmentals per language and would be the most modern first-hand statement.

sources.citation: Marrison, Geoffrey E. 1967. The classification of the Naga languages of North East India. PhD dissertation, SOAS, University of London. 2 vols (292+460 pp.).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Vol. I has per-language phonological summaries (including tone) for 31 Naga varieties including Meluri (Pochuri); its Meluri data derive from Mills 1937, so a stress statement is unlikely but it is the standard comparative reference and is deposited open-access at SOAS Research Online, which our network cannot resolve.
